sections.heading: Application documents, testing and license conditions
sections.markdown:
## C — Application documents, testing and license conditions

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A17
A Nebraska application requires at least 2 documents establishing the principal address. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A17
An applicant must disclose a verifiable Social Security number or establish the specified exemption with a valid arrival-and-departure record in a valid foreign passport. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A17
New Nebraska applicants must provide citizenship proof when applying. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A17
After citizenship proof has been presented, it is not required again at later licensing-office visits. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A17
An applicant who is not a U.S. citizen must present lawful-status proof on every licensing-office visit. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A17
Required documents must be certified and bear a raised seal or stamp. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A17
A faxed document or photocopy is not accepted for the application. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A17
Document review may require more information and a later office visit rather than same-day approval. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A17
A document marked as unsuitable for identification proof cannot establish identity. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A17
The DMV may keep copies of documents submitted with an application. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A17
A name-change applicant must supply certified records linking the current license name with the new name. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A17
A state-government-certified birth certificate is an accepted citizenship-and-identity document. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A17
A birth certificate from a hospital is not accepted. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A17
A Puerto Rico birth certificate issued before September 30, 2010 is not accepted. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A17
An unexpired U.S. passport or passport card can establish citizenship and identity. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A17
A valid arrival-and-departure record in a valid foreign passport can establish lawful status and identity under the handbook’s listed conditions. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A17
Student or exchange statuses identified in the handbook require additional school or exchange records to supply SEVIS information. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A17
A foreign passport is unnecessary for the listed arrival record when it is stamped Refugee or the person’s place of origin is Canada. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A17
A visa alone is not one of the accepted lawful-status and identity documents listed here. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A18
An unexpired permanent-resident card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A18
An unexpired employment-authorization card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A18
The listed naturalization certificate can establish citizenship and identity. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A18
The listed citizenship certificate can establish citizenship and identity. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A18
The listed State Department consular birth-abroad report can establish citizenship and identity. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A18
Principal-address evidence must show the Nebraska address and come from 2 different issuing sources. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A18
A post-office box does not establish the principal residence address. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A18
An applicant younger than 21 who cannot supply personal residence proof may use the parent’s or guardian’s address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A18
A bank or other financial-institution statement used for residence proof must have been issued within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A18
A pay stub used for residence proof must be from the preceding 90 days and show the employer’s name and address. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A18
A government document used under the handbook’s recent-document category must have been issued within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A18
A magazine used for residence proof must be from the preceding 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A18
A mailed envelope, box or postcard used as address proof must show a postmark or stamped date within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A18
Correspondence, a receipt or an invoice used in the recent-address-document category must be dated within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A18
A valid Nebraska vehicle registration is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A18
A valid insurance policy or card for life, health, auto or home coverage is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A18
A valid real-estate tax statement or receipt is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A18
A valid license is among the documents accepted to establish residence. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A18
A Nebraska voter-registration card is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A18
A lease or rental agreement used for residence proof must give the landlord’s name and contact information. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A18
A mortgage agreement is among the accepted principal-address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A18
A Nebraska DMV renewal notice is among the accepted principal-address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A18
A blank check or deposit slip is among the accepted principal-address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A18
If Social Security proof is requested, it must show the complete number. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A18
The DMV verifies Social Security numbers and documents from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A18
A Social Security card is an accepted form of Social Security proof. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A18
A wage-and-tax statement is among the listed Social Security proof documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F47 | anchor: A18
A Social Security benefit tax statement is among the listed Social Security proof documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

Misconceptions: Passing a drive test does not remove identification requirements or license restrictions.
Mnemonics: Documents, vision, written, drive: check each requirement for the applicable path.
Glossary: Principal address means the applicant’s Nebraska residence address; a restriction limits the licensed driving privilege.
Dynamic facts: Changing contacts, officials, live services and fees are withheld from the stable rule inventory.
